title: The Panchavati
introduction: Rama entrusts the construction work of a parNa shaala, straw-cottage in Panchavati, nearby river Godavari. Lakshmana with all his expertise constructs a cosy cottage and they enter it after the ritual of house-entering ceremony. Rama admires Lakshmana for his construction work and as a thanksgiving he embraces Lakshmana and expresses his heart felt feeling about Lakshmana's concern towards Rama.
closing: इति वाल्मीकि रामायणे आदि काव्ये अरण्य काण्डे पंचदशः सर्गः
Thus, this is the 15th chapter in Aranya Kanda of Valmiki Ramayana, the First Epic poem of India.

verses.devanagari:
ततः पंचवटीम् गत्वा नाना व्याल मृगायुताम् |
उवाच भ्रातरम् रामो लक्ष्मणम् दीप्त तेजसम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ paṃcavaṭīm gatvā nānā vyāla mṛgāyutām |
uvāca bhrātaram rāmo lakṣmaṇam dīpta tejasam
verses.translation: Then on going to Panchavati which is full with many serpents and predators, Rama said to splendidly brilliant Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: to one who is splendidly, brilliant, to brother, to Lakshmana, said.

verses.devanagari:
आगताः स्म यथा उद्दिष्टम् यम् देशम् मुनिः अब्रवीत् |
अयम् पंचवटी देशः सौम्य पुष्पित काननः
verses.iast:
āgatāḥ sma yathā uddiṣṭam yam deśam muniḥ abravīt |
ayam paṃcavaṭī deśaḥ saumya puṣpita kānanaḥ
verses.translation: "We arrived at the place as indicated by the sage, oh, gentle Lakshmana, this region with its flowered forests is Panchavati."

glosses.meaning: with flowered, forests, this, region is, Panchavati.

verses.devanagari:
सर्वतः चार्यताम् दृष्टिः कानने निपुणो हि असि |
आश्रमः कतर अस्मिन् नः देशे भवति सम्मतः
verses.iast:
sarvataḥ cāryatām dṛṣṭiḥ kānane nipuṇo hi asi |
āśramaḥ katara asmin naḥ deśe bhavati sammataḥ
verses.translation: "In which place we have to situate our hermitage for our liking, for that cast your sight all over the forest, and indeed you are an expert in such matters.

glosses.itrans: katarasmin deshe naH aashramaH sammataH bhavati
glosses.iast: katarasmin deśe naḥ āśramaḥ sammataḥ bhavati
glosses.devanagari: कतरस्मिन् देशे नः आश्रमः सम्मतः भवति
glosses.meaning: in which, place, to us, hermitage, agreeable [to our liking,] it will be
in forest, everywhere, your sight, be cast about for

verses.devanagari:
रमते यत्र वैदेही त्वम् अहम् चैव लक्ष्मण |
तादृशो दृश्यताम् देशः संनिकृष्ट जलाशयः
वन रामण्यकम् यत्र जल रामण्यकम् तथा |
संनिकृष्टम् च यस्मिन् तु समित् पुष्प कुश उदकम्
verses.iast:
ramate yatra vaidehī tvam aham caiva lakṣmaṇa |
tādṛśo dṛśyatām deśaḥ saṃnikṛṣṭa jalāśayaḥ
vana rāmaṇyakam yatra jala rāmaṇyakam tathā |
saṃnikṛṣṭam ca yasmin tu samit puṣpa kuśa udakam
verses.translation: "In which place Vaidehi, likewise you and me too can take delight, where the woodland is scenic and the water is pleasurable, and where a water lake, ritual-firewood, flowers, and the sacred grass are available in proximity, oh, Lakshmana, such a place may be searched out.
notes: Other versions read the jala rāmaṇyakam as sthala rāmaṇyakam. Rama desires a place that shall be scenic with flower gardens where Seetha can easily pluck flowers in those gardens. And it shall be a pleasurable garden for him to recline, or take his bath etc., and thirdly it shall contain the ritual paraphernalia within the reach of Lakshmana, so that Lakshmana can provide them to Rama in time, with his obedient service.

glosses.itrans: yasmin tu samit puSpa kusha udakam
glosses.iast: yasmin tu samit puṣpa kuśa udakam
glosses.devanagari: यस्मिन् तु समित् पुष्प कुश उदकं
glosses.meaning: wherein, ritual firewood, flowers, darbha grass, water
very, nearby, water, receptacle [will be there]

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण लक्मणः संयत अंजलिः |
सीता समक्षम् काकुत्स्थम् इदम् वचनम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
evam uk{}taḥ tu rāmeṇa lakmaṇaḥ saṃyata aṃjaliḥ |
sītā samakṣam kākutstham idam vacanam abravīt
verses.translation: When thus said by Rama, Lakshmana adjoined his palms and said this sentence to Rama in the presence of Seetha.

glosses.meaning: by Rama, thus, one who is said, Lakshmana

verses.devanagari:
परवान् अस्मि काकुत्स्थ त्वयि वर्ष शतम् स्थिते |
स्वयम् तु रुचिरे देशे क्रियताम् इति माम् वद
verses.iast:
paravān asmi kākutstha tvayi varṣa śatam sthite |
svayam tu rucire deśe kriyatām iti mām vada
verses.translation: "I am but a dependent, as long as you are there, may it be for innumerable years, I am your adherent, Rama, therefore you yourself tell me to build hermitage in such and such delightful place.
notes: Lakshmana is an ever adherent of the Supreme Vishnu as he is the thousand-headed serpent namely ādi śeṣa, on which Vishnu reclines. Even in this incarnation of Rama, Lakshmana says he is the same adherent. Thus Lakshmana wants Rama not to say 'you do it your way' but to order 'you do it my way.' Further, Lakshmana is saying this in presence of Seetha, sītā samakṣe, because if she is not going to accept that place, Rama rejects it. Hence, it firstly is the choice of Seetha on which Rama's approval will be automatic. Thus the question of agreeability or disagreeability of Lakshmana does not arise. 'Even in this incarnation in the dynasty of Kakutstha as Rama, I am still subservient to you, as I was in vaikuṇṭha , as ādi śeṣa . And this tvayi varṣa śatam sthite : śata is lexically a hundred but also used in its infinitude, thus 'I am anytime servant of yours.' svayam tu rucire deśe : 'Your choice of place is but my pleasure.' This is to portray the self-denial of Lakshmana, apart from any individual identity let alone the devotee status, total dedication kainkarya, to the Supreme. This is according to Govindaraja.

Adherent nature of Lakshmana is also like that of a younger brother towards his elder brother, for the elder brother becomes father-like after the demise of their father. anenapiturantaram yāvat jyeṣṭho jīvati tāvat kaniṣṭhasya na svātantryam itisūcitam | tathā ca manuḥ piteva pālayat sutān jyeṣṭha bhrātā yavīyasaḥ | putravat ca api varteran jyeṣṭho bhrātari dharmataḥ || dharmākūtam.

glosses.meaning: you, years, hundred [innumerable,] while you are there

verses.devanagari:
सुप्रीतः तेन वाक्येन लक्ष्मणस्य महाद्युतिः |
विमृशन् रोचयामास देशम् सर्व गुण अन्वितम्
verses.iast:
suprītaḥ tena vākyena lakṣmaṇasya mahādyutiḥ |
vimṛśan rocayāmāsa deśam sarva guṇa anvitam
verses.translation: Rama is gladdened by those words of that great resplendent Lakshmana, and he selected a place that comprised of all the attributes.

glosses.meaning: by the great, resplendence, Lakshmana's, by that, wording
a place, started to like [to select.]

verses.devanagari:
स तम् रुचिरम् आक्रम्य देशम् आश्रम कर्मणि |
हस्ते गृहीत्वा हस्तेन रामः सौमित्रिम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
sa tam ruciram ākramya deśam āśrama ka.rmaṇi |
haste gṛhītvā hastena rāmaḥ saumitrim abravīt
verses.translation: On taking Lakshmana's hand by his hand Rama paced that beautiful place intended for the construction of hermitage up and down and spoke to Soumitri this way.

glosses.meaning: by hand, Soumitri's, hand, on taking

verses.devanagari:
अयम् देशः समः श्रीमान् पुष्पितैर् तरुभिर् वृतः |
इह आश्रम पदम् सौम्य यथावत् कर्तुम् अर्हसि
verses.iast:
ayam deśaḥ samaḥ śrīmān puṣpitair tarubhir vṛtaḥ |
iha āśrama padam saumya yathāvat kartum arhasi
verses.translation: "This is an evenly and propitious place surrounded with flowered trees and it is apt of you to erect hermitage here, traditionally.

glosses.itrans: iha yathaavat aashrama padam kartum arhasi
glosses.iast: iha yathāvat āśrama padam kartum arhasi
glosses.devanagari: इह यथावत् आश्रम पदं कर्तुं अर्हसि
glosses.meaning: here, traditionally, hermitage, to erect, apt of you.

verses.devanagari:
इयम् आदित्य संकाशैः पद्मैः सुरभि गंधिभिः |
अदूरे दृश्यते रम्या पद्मिनी पद्म शोभिता
verses.iast:
iyam āditya saṅkāśaiḥ padmaiḥ surabhi gaṃdhibhiḥ |
adūre dṛśyate ramyā padminī padma śobhitā
verses.translation: "This pleasing lake is seen here adjacently, beaming forth with its lotuses that are similar to sun in resplendence, and that are scented fragrantly.
notes: The Lake is beaming with lotuses that have the resplendence of Sun. Sun is Vishnu's another aspect, sūrya nārāyaṇa , and hence that Vishnu is here in the form of lake. The lotus is the abode of Goddess Lakshmi and the lake is full with such lotuses, which are in the heart of the lake. As such Goddess Lakshmi is in the lotuses, which again are situated in the heart of Vishnu, and hence this is a propitious lake to have Vishnu and Lakshmi together.

verses.devanagari:
यथा आख्यातम् अगस्त्येन मुनिना भावितात्मना |
इयम् गोदावरी रम्या पुष्पितैः तरुभिर् वृता
हंस कारण्डव आकीर्णा चक्रवाक उपशोभिता |
verses.iast:
yathā ākhyātam agastyena muninā bhāvitātmanā |
iyam godāvarī ramyā puṣpitaiḥ tarubhir vṛtā
haṃsa kāraṇḍava ākīrṇā cakravāka upaśobhitā |
verses.translation: "This River Godavari is also seen from here, surrounded by blooming trees, spread over with swans, and beautified with kaarandava, and chakravaaka birds, as that contemplated soul sage Agastya had said.

glosses.meaning: by contemplated soul, by sage, Agastya
this, river Godavari is [also seen from here.]

verses.devanagari:
न अतिदूरे न च आसन्ने मृग यूथ निपीडिता
मयूर नादिता रम्याः प्रांशवो बहु कंदराः |
दृश्यन्ते गिरयः सौम्य फुल्लैः तरुभिर् आवृताः
verses.iast:
na atidūre na ca āsanne mṛga yūtha nipīḍitā
mayūra nāditā ramyāḥ prāṃśavo bahu kaṃdarāḥ |
dṛśyante girayaḥ saumya phullaiḥ tarubhir āvṛtāḥ
verses.translation: "Those soaring mountains are appearing beautiful with many caves, surrounded by flowered trees, flurried by animal herds, sounded by peacocks, and they are neither far-off nor very nearby.

verses.devanagari:
सौवर्णै राजतैः ताम्रैः देशे देशे च धातुभिः |
गवाक्षिता इव आभान्ति गजाः परम भक्तिभिः
verses.iast:
sauvarṇai rājataiḥ tāmraiḥ deśe deśe ca dhātubhiḥ |
gavākṣitā iva ābhānti gajāḥ parama bhak{}tibhiḥ
verses.translation: "Here and there are the golden, silvery and coppery ores on the mountains, and they are shining forth like cow-eye ventilators on walls and also like the superb paintings on elephants.
notes: The gava akśa is cow-eye, meaning the cow-eye shaped ventilators of walls. The bhakti is the name for coloured graphical drawings on the body of elephants. Apart from the howdah and other ornamentations, the elephants are richly painted in colours during ceremonial occasions, even today. As such Rama is visualising the ore deposits on the mountains as cow-eye like ventilators on walls, and as superb streaks of paintings on the bodies of elephants.

verses.devanagari:
सालैः तालैः तमालैः च खर्जूरैः पनसैः द्रुमैः |
नीवारैः तिनिशैः चैव पुन्नागैः च उपशोभिताः
चूतैर् अशोकैः तिलकैः केतकैर् अपि चंपकैः |
पुष्प गुल्म लता उपेतैः तैः तैः तरुभिर् आवृताः
स्यन्दनैः चंदनैः नीपैः पर्णासैः लकुचैः अपि |
धव अश्वकर्ण खदिरैः शमी किंशुक पाटलैः
verses.iast:
sālaiḥ tālaiḥ tamālaiḥ ca khar.hjūraiḥ panasaiḥ drumaiḥ |
nīvāraiḥ tiniśaiḥ caiva punnāgaiḥ ca upaśobhitāḥ
cūtair aśokaiḥ tilakaiḥ ketakair api campakaiḥ |
puṣpa gulma latā upetaiḥ taiḥ taiḥ tarubhir āvṛtāḥ
syandanaiḥ caṃdanaiḥ nīpaiḥ pa.rṇāsaiḥ lakucaiḥ api |
dhava aśvakarṇa khadiraiḥ śamī kiṃśuka pāṭalaiḥ
verses.translation: "These mountains are brightening with trees of Saala, Palmyra, Tamaala, Date Palms, Jackfruit and also thus with Punnaagaa. With Chuuta - Sweet Mango; Ashoka, Tialaka, even with Ketaka, Champaka trees, And even with Syandana, Sandalwood, Niipa, Paarnasa, Lakuch, dhava, Ashwakarna, Khadira, Shamii, Kimshuka, Paatala trees, and entwined are those and those trees with flowered shrubs, and along with climbers, and thus they brighten the mountains.

glosses.meaning: Niivaara [wild grain,] Tinisha [Dolbergia Oujeinesis,] also thus
those, those, trees, entwined. syandanaiH candanaiH niipaiH = Syandana, Sandalwood, Niipa

verses.devanagari:
इदम् पुण्यम् इदम् रम्यम् इदम् बहु मृग द्विजम् |
इह वत्स्याम सौमित्रे सार्धम् एतेन पक्षिणा
verses.iast:
idam puṇyam idam ramyam idam bahu mṛga dvijam |
iha vatsyāma saumitre sārdham etena pakṣiṇā
verses.translation: "This place is holy, this is delightful and this is with many animals and birds, hence Soumitri, let us reside here along with this bird Jatayu." Thus said Rama to Lakshmana.

glosses.meaning: this, is holy, this, is delightful

verses.devanagari:
एवम् उक्तः तु रामेण लक्ष्मणः परवीरहा |
अचिरेण आश्रमम् भ्रातुः चकार सुमहाबलः
verses.iast:
evam uk{}taḥ tu rāmeṇa lakṣmaṇaḥ paravīrahā |
acireṇa āśramam bhrātuḥ cakāra sumahābalaḥ
verses.translation: Thus said by Rama to that remover of foe's valour and one with very great might, namely Lakshmana, he briskly erected a hermitage for his brother.

glosses.meaning: thus, who is said, by Rama
very, great, mighty one [Lakshmana] a cireNa = without, delay [briskly]

verses.devanagari:
पर्णशालाम् सुविपुलाम् तत्र संघात मृत्तिकाम् |
सुस्तंभाम् मस्करैर् दीर्घैः कृत वंशाम् सुशोभनाम्
शमी शाखाभिः आस्तीर्य धृढ पाशावपाशितम् |
कुश काश शरैः पर्णैः सुपरिच्छ्हादिताम् तथा
समीकृत तलाम् रम्याम् चकार सुमहाबलः |
निवासम् राघवस्य अर्थे प्रेक्ष्णीयम् अनुत्तमम्
verses.iast:
parṇaśālām suvipulām tatra saṅghāta mṛttikām |
sustambhām maskarair dīrghaiḥ kṛta vaṃśām suśobhanām
śamī śākhābhiḥ āstīrya dhṛḍha pāśāvapāśitam |
kuśa kāśa śaraiḥ parṇaiḥ suparicchhāditām tathā
samīkṛta talām ramyām cakāra sumahābalaḥ |
nivāsam rāghavasya arthe prekśṇīyam anuttamam
verses.translation: Lakshmana built a very spacious straw-cottage there levelling and raising the clay for raised floor of the cottage, strongly pillared with long bamboos, thereupon on those pillars excellent rafters are made, and the branches of Shamii trees are spread out, twined firmly with twines of jute strands, and with the cross-laid bamboos for thatching, and over that blades of Kusha grass and leaves of Kaasha are spread and well over-covered for the roof, and thus that very great mighty Lakshmana made that best and very spacious straw-cottage with a levelled surface for residence of Raghava in the interests of Raghava alone, and it resulted as a feast to the eye.

glosses.meaning: well, dug up, clay raising platform
with Shamii trees, branches, spread out
Kusha, Kaasha, grass blades [Saccharum spontaneum], leaves
sightly one [feast to eye,] the best one

verses.devanagari:
स गत्वा लक्ष्मणः श्रीमान् नदीम् गोदावरीम् तदा |
स्नात्वा पद्मानि च आदाय सफलः पुनर् आगतः
verses.iast:
sa gatvā lakṣmaṇaḥ śrīmān nadīm godāvarīm tadā |
snātvā padmāni ca ādāya saphalaḥ punar āgataḥ
verses.translation: On his going to River Godavari that noble Lakshmana bathed and on gathering lotuses and fruits he returned to the cottage.

glosses.itrans: nadiim godaavariim snaatvaa padmaani ca aadaaya
glosses.iast: nadīm godāvarīm snātvā padmāni ca ādāya
glosses.devanagari: नदीं गोदावरीं स्नात्वा पद्मानि च आदाय
glosses.meaning: to river, Godavari, bathed, lotuses, also, gathered

verses.devanagari:
ततः पुष्प बलिम् कृत्वा शान्तिम् च स यथाविधि |
दर्शयामास रामाय तद् आश्रम पदम् कृतम्
verses.iast:
tataḥ puṣpa balim kṛtvā śāntim ca sa yathāvidhi |
darśayāmāsa rāmāya tad āśrama padam kṛtam
verses.translation: Then making flowery offerings and peace-invocations also procedural to gR^iha pravesha , entering a new house,] started to show the constructed hermitage to Rama.

glosses.meaning: peace invocations also procedurally on making
that which is built, that, hermitage

verses.devanagari:
स तम् दृष्ट्वा कृतम् सौम्यम् आश्रमम् सह सीतया |
राघवः पर्णशालायाम् हर्षम् आहारयत् परम्
verses.iast:
sa tam dṛṣṭvā kṛtam saumyam āśramam saha sītayā |
rāghavaḥ parṇaśālāyām harṣam āhārayat param
verses.translation: On seeing the beautifully constructed hermitage along with Seetha, Rama is highly gladdened in respect that straw-cottage.

glosses.meaning: that, constructed, beautiful, hermitage, on seeing

verses.devanagari:
सुसंहृष्टः परिष्वज्य बाहुभ्याम् लक्ष्मणम् तदा |
अति स्निग्धम् च गाढम् च वचनम् च इदम् अब्रवीत्
verses.iast:
susaṃhṛṣṭaḥ pariṣvajya bāhubhyām lakṣmaṇam tadā |
ati snigdham ca gāḍham ca vacanam ca idam abravīt
verses.translation: Then Rama very highly gladdened Rama embraced Lakshmana tightly by both of his hands, and spoke these friendly words to him.

glosses.meaning: Lakshmana is, with both arms, tightly, on embracing

verses.devanagari:
प्रीतो अस्मि ते महत् कर्म त्वया कृतम् इदम् प्रभो |
प्रदेयो यन् निमित्तम् ते परिष्व.ंगो मया कृतः
verses.iast:
prīto asmi te mahat karma tvayā kṛtam idam prabho |
pradeyo yan nimittam te pariṣva.ṃgo mayā kṛtaḥ
verses.translation: "Oh, masterful one, I am very happy about you for you have done a great deed, for that reason I am giving what I have to give to you a hugging.

glosses.meaning: by you, a great, deed, is done

verses.devanagari:
भावज्ञेन कृतज्ञेन धर्मज्ञेन च लक्ष्मण |
त्वया पुत्रेण धर्मात्मा न संवृत्तः पिता मम
verses.iast:
bhāvajñena kṛtajñena dharmajñena ca lakṣmaṇa |
tvayā putreṇa dharmātmā na saṃvṛttaḥ pitā mama
verses.translation: "You are the knower of others feelings, knower of many skills, and the knower of what is right and honest, oh, Lakshmana, such as you are, being with you I deem that my virtue-souled father is not gone and forgotten.
notes: The word bhāvajñaḥ means here as the knower of other's feelings. Lakshmana is well aware of such things while talking with sages, his brothers, his mothers and his ministers like Hanuma and other subjects. Here also Lakshmana knew the feelings of Rama as to how the cottage is envisioned by Rama, with due privacy to Rama and Seetha, with a porch, worship-room, and an accommodation for himself. kṛtajña is masterly craftsmanship and flair for doing all deeds of sublime nature, but not 'faithful' in routine sense. dharmajñaḥ is knower of honesty. Though he himself is a prince, Lakshmana did not construct the cottage for his comfort, but the convenience of Rama and Seetha are counted firstly. The word dharmātmā , virtue souled one, can also be prefixed to Dasharatha like dharmātmā mama pitā virtue-souled, my, father, meaning that 'the virtue-souled Dasharatha has left you behind him for my sake, because you are arranging all the things for me, as a father would naturally do for his son.' The word sam vṛttaḥ in the observation of Dr. Satya Vrat in his book 'The Ramayana - A Linguistic Study is:-- This word has been found used in a rather remarkable sense [in Ramayana.] It is 'to die'. sam vṛttaḥ means dead. Ordinarily samvṛttaḥ has quite the opposite sense, viz., 'born', i.e., father Dasharatha took rebirth as Lakshmana, to provide for the needs of Rama.

And Dharmaakuutam says that, anena mṛte api pitādhārmikeṇa putreṇa amṛta iti sūcitam | tathā ca vājasaneya brāhmaṇañ-- 'saputreṇa eva asmin loke pratitiṣṭhati -- ' iti | sa ca pitā svayam mṛte apidhārmiksya putrasy śarīreṇa eva asmin loke yathā śāstram karma kurvan tiṣṭhatīti artham || dhamākūtam Hence Rama said in this concept also that - 'my father is though 'dead', but 'born' again in you, Lakshmana.'

glosses.meaning: my, virtue-souled, father, is not, gone and forgotten.

verses.devanagari:
एवम् लक्ष्मणम् उक्त्वा तु राघवो लक्ष्मिवर्धनः |
तस्मिन् देशे बहु फले न्यवसत् स सुखम् सुखी
verses.iast:
evam lakṣmaṇam uk{}tvā tu rāghavo lakṣmivardhanaḥ |
tasmin deśe bahu phale nyavasat sa sukham sukhī
verses.translation: On saying thus to Lakshmana, Raghava, the enhancer of magnificence comfortably resided in that province which is with many a fruit.
notes: The last word sukhī is read as vaśī in other mms meaning that Rama 'with his senses controlled' lived there. That is to suggest the overcoming of the enchantment of Suurpanakha.

glosses.meaning: contented one [one who controlled his senses, Rama]
in that, province, with many, fruits

verses.devanagari:
कंचित् कालम् स धर्मात्मा सीतया लक्ष्मणेन च
अन्वास्यमानो न्यवसत् स्वर्ग लोके यथा अमरः
verses.iast:
kañcit kālam sa dharmātmā sītayā lakṣmaṇena ca
anvāsyamāno nyavasat svarga loke yathā amaraḥ
verses.translation: While Seetha and Lakshmana devoted themselves to that righteous Rama, he resided in Panchavati like a Divinity in heavenly world for sometime to come.

glosses.meaning: that righteous one, he that Rama
for some, time, he resided there.
